fieldValues.title: The essay editor offers visual formatting over plain markdown, and the writer can always switch to the source
fieldValues.move: In the essay editor, clicking a paragraph opens it as formatted text with a small toolbar, so a writer can format without knowing markdown. An existing library provides the editing surface, limited to a short allowlist. The stored text stays plain markdown the writer can read and take away, the core stays the only renderer for reading, and a per-browser switch returns the writer to the source editor. The core renderer judges each round trip: a paragraph it cannot reproduce opens as source, and a paragraph opened and left is not rewritten. The help says plainly that paragraphs are markdown. It applies to the essay editor only: elsewhere, types and fields carry the structure.
fieldValues.does_not_fix: Other editors and record forms, which keep plain text by design. Images and tables in the visual editor, which stay source-only for now. Byte-for-byte preservation of an edited paragraph: an edit normalises that paragraph's markup without changing how it reads. Whether a writer understands the essay's structure of titled, nested paragraphs (SP-130).
fieldValues.falsifier: A first-time writer given only the link still cannot format a paragraph unaided; or a paragraph saved from the visual editor reads differently from what the writer saw; or writers mostly switch to markdown because the visual editor gets in the way.
